target_customer: universities and campus groups that would pay for a hosted version of the Turf campus game, plus students as players
problem: Campuses lack a shared, fun activity that engages students campus wide. Turf offered a weeks long Risk style game that uses the campus map.
business_model: game run as a service for institutions (per YC description); revenue sources not detailed
product_category: social online game for college campuses

founders.name: Andrew Fong
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; TechCrunch ties him to Harvard.

founders.name: Matthew O'Brien
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; TechCrunch ties him to Harvard.

founders.name: Gabe Smedresman
founders.role: Founder, creator of the original Turf game
founders.background_notes: Named as a Kirkland North founder in TechCrunch and Xconomy March 2008, not on the YC page. Started the Turf experiment at Yale in January 2007.

founders.name: Hugo Van Vuuren
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in TechCrunch March 2008 and quoted on usage; not on the YC page.

exit.reason: No shutdown or acquisition announcement found; YC lists the company as Inactive.

competitors.name: GoCrossCampus
competitors.what: Risk style online game played by campus sections, founded by Yale and Columbia students and inspired by the same original game
competitors.traction_then: Its Yale game drew over 3,300 students; about 20 games run, per its cofounder

technical_complexity.rationale: A persistent multiplayer territory game had to handle thousands of simultaneous players per campus; Kirkland North reported a Stanford game with 2,500 players and its rival claimed technical failures in some of its games.

defensibility.rationale: A direct rival with a separately written codebase appeared at the same time, and the game concept came from a one off campus experiment.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent was found competing; the main threat was a peer startup.

market_need_then: Facebook had made online campus social life mainstream by 2008, and the original Turf game drew over 3,300 Yale students in 2007, showing player demand. Demand from paying institutions is not documented.

branding.domain_note: kirklandnorth.com; no purchase history found. The host did not resolve when fetched.
branding.brand_signature: Turf, the game name, was the consumer facing brand rather than the company name
branding.community_and_virality: Turf spread through campus competition (Yale 2007, Stanford 2008) and press covered the dispute with GoCrossCampus.

brand_strength.rationale: Press mentions in TechCrunch and Xconomy centred on Turf and the rivalry; the company name itself had little recognition.

outcome_analysis: Kirkland North turned a student run campus game into a service and ran six games by March 2008, including a Stanford game with 2,500 players. It faced a near identical rival, GoCrossCampus, that also claimed the idea. YC now lists it as Inactive, but no shutdown story, funding amount or cause was found, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: The YC description says the game ran at Yale and Harvard; press says it began at Yale and the company debuted a Stanford game in February 2008. Xconomy could not be fetched (503), so its details come only from the search snippet. Founder education beyond Smedresman was not found.
